questions.subject: DISCRETE_MATHEMATICS_II
questions.learningObjective: Solve an exam-level problem in discrete mathematics from first principles.
questions.stem: How many Boolean functions exist on 2 variables? (case 33)
questions.explanation: There are 2^2=4 input rows and each can map to 0 or 1, so there are 2^4=16 functions. Counting only rows confuses the domain size with the number of functions.
questions.hint: Two to the number of truth-table rows.

questions.subject: DISCRETE_MATHEMATICS_II
questions.learningObjective: Solve an exam-level problem in discrete mathematics from first principles.
questions.stem: How many binary relations are there on a set with 4 elements?
questions.explanation: A relation is any subset of the n^2 ordered pairs, so there are 2^(4^2)=65536 relations. Counting functions or subsets of the set gives a much smaller number.
questions.hint: A relation is a subset of the Cartesian product.

questions.subject: DISCRETE_MATHEMATICS_II
questions.learningObjective: Solve an exam-level problem in discrete mathematics from first principles.
questions.stem: How many binary relations are there on a set with 4 elements? (case 12)
questions.explanation: A relation is any subset of the n^2 ordered pairs, so there are 2^(4^2)=65536 relations. Counting functions or subsets of the set gives a much smaller number.
questions.hint: A relation is a subset of the Cartesian product.

questions.stem: How many Boolean functions exist on 2 variables? (case 51)
questions.explanation: There are 2^2=4 input rows and each can map to 0 or 1, so there are 2^4=16 functions. Counting only rows confuses the domain size with the number of functions.
questions.hint: Two to the number of truth-table rows.
